research.summary: Workspace-only review of planning docs and implementation found a real CivicState civic-letter product, stale/inconsistent planning status, unvalidated market claims, and a watchlist registry posture.
methods: Read existing soul/planning docs before writing root soul.
Marked all external market, competitor, conversion, and valuation claims as assumptions because no network research was available.
Built bottom-up TAM/SAM/SOM and three-year financial model from implemented pricing tiers and explicit assumptions.

planningMethod.evidenceHarvest: Preserved true claims from planning docs and implementation files.
planningMethod.marketResearch: Used bottom-up assumptions only; no external research performed.
planningMethod.financialValidation: Reconciled revenue as paid submissions x blended AOV plus staged organization pilots.
planningMethod.alternativeSearch: Compared consumer civic transaction, organization advocacy workflow, generic AI drafting, and research-asset options.
planningMethod.antiPlan: Killed weak claims around demand, deliverability, citation relevance, compliance readiness, and venture scale.
planningMethod.finalSynthesis: WAIT for operator merge and market validation before roadmap or investibility authority.

segments.name: Individual US constituents
segments.painfulJob: Need to turn a civic concern into a researched, routed, compliant letter without knowing law, jurisdiction, or official contacts.

segments.name: Future civic organizations
segments.painfulJob: Need repeated campaign research, drafting, delivery, and status tracking after the individual pipeline proves quality.

currentSubstitutes: Resistbot or similar free advocacy tools [assumption: model-knowledge competitor].
Quorum/FiscalNote/VoterVoice style organization advocacy suites [assumption: model-knowledge competitor].
Generic AI drafting in ChatGPT or Claude [assumption: model-knowledge substitute].
willingnessToPayEvidence: $5/$15/$25 tiers are implemented in the payment route [evidence: apps/api/src/routes/payments.ts].
No paid demand is validated yet [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md says validated requirements are none].
Preview-to-paid conversion must be tested at >=3% [assumption: validation gate from .planning/PROJECT.md].

market.category: Consumer civic-tech workflow with possible organization/API expansion.
market.competitiveLandscape: Free civic-action bots, enterprise advocacy CRMs, generic AI assistants, manual email, consultants, and legal help solve parts of the workflow.
market.wedge: Start with paid individual constituent letters; expand only if demand, delivery, and citation evidence justify an organization/API wedge.
market.tam: $15,000,000 annual gross bookings from 1,000,000 assumed paid civic-letter submissions x $15 blended AOV [assumption: bottom-up model].
market.sam: $750,000 annual gross bookings from 50,000 reachable submissions x $15 blended AOV [assumption: reachable organic wedge].
market.som: $36,000 annual gross bookings from 2,400 first-year paid submissions x $15 blended AOV [assumption: single-operator case].

businessModel.valueCreation: Collapse jurisdiction lookup, legal-source research, citation verification, professional drafting, payment, delivery, and tracking into one paid workflow.
businessModel.valueDelivery: Self-serve web wizard backed by API routes, BullMQ workers, legal-source integrations, Stripe, Postmark, dashboards, and admin review.
businessModel.valueCapture: $5 one-off, $15 three-pack, and $25 full-spread campaign tiers [evidence: apps/api/src/routes/payments.ts].
businessModel.pricing: $15 blended AOV assumed from the implemented $5/$15/$25 tiers [assumption: tier mix].
businessModel.revenuePath: Consumer paid campaigns first; organization/API pilots only after validation.
businessModel.unitEconomics: 90%+ contribution margin before support if variable costs stay near $0.20/$0.40/$0.60 per tier [assumption: tests/payment.test.ts cost references, not invoice evidence].
businessModel.operatingCosts: Hosting/tooling, model calls, email delivery, official-data provider, moderation, citation review, support, and compliance maintenance.
businessModel.marginLogic: Low variable cost is plausible, but human review and deliverability support can overwhelm low AOV.

financialModel.summary: Base case reaches $57,000 revenue in 2027 and $300,000 revenue in 2028 only if consumer flow works and organization pilots begin [assumption: model].
financialModel.validationStatus: Needs operator/market validation; not approved for roadmap authority.
revenueAssumptions: 200 paid submissions x $15 blended AOV produces $3,000 in 2026 launch revenue [assumption].
3,000 paid submissions x $15 plus 2 organization pilots x $6,000/year produces $57,000 in 2027 revenue [assumption].
12,000 paid submissions x $15 plus 10 organization pilots x $12,000/year produces $300,000 in 2028 revenue [assumption].
costAssumptions: Hosting/tooling starts from the prior $132.50/month planning burn and scales upward [evidence: .planning/PROJECT.md; assumption: scale].
Variable cost remains below $0.60 per campaign in base case [assumption: tests/payment.test.ts cost references].
Support and human review are the dominant cost risk if moderation or citation exceptions are frequent [assumption].
sensitivityTests: If 2027 paid submissions are only 1,000 x $15 with no pilots, revenue is $15,000 [assumption: bear case].
If human review averages $8 per paid campaign, $5 and $15 tiers are likely unattractive [assumption: support stress].
If preview-to-paid conversion is under 3%, self-serve consumer scaling pauses [assumption: demand gate].
If .gov inbox placement is under 85%, paid delivery is not credible [assumption: deliverability gate].

alternatives.name: Consumer civic-letter transaction
alternatives.thesis: Individuals will pay a small fee for research, drafting, routing, and delivery.
alternatives.expectedUpside: Low variable cost and data compounding if volume exists.
alternatives.rejectionOrSelectionRationale: Selected as current repo reality, but demand is unproven.

alternatives.name: Organization advocacy workflow
alternatives.thesis: Small civic groups may pay recurring fees for repeated workflows.
alternatives.rejectionOrSelectionRationale: Deferred until consumer quality and deliverability are proven.

alternatives.name: Research asset only
alternatives.thesis: The code and planning are useful as a personal/research asset, not a venture.
alternatives.rejectionOrSelectionRationale: Still plausible because registry note says personal/research and not near-term investible.

antiPlan.summary: The plan fails if users will not pay, officials do not receive the emails, citations are not substantively reliable, or the operator never approves business posture.

holes.hole: Users may prefer free AI drafts or free civic tools over paying.
holes.whyItMatters: Low AOV leaves little room for CAC or support.
holes.repair: Run paid preview tests and pause if conversion is under 3% [assumption].

holes.hole: Government email deliverability may be too weak.
holes.whyItMatters: A paid delivery product cannot sell messages that land in spam.
holes.repair: Require .gov inbox placement tests, bounce tracking, SPF/DKIM/DMARC, and warming evidence.

holes.hole: Citation verification can verify existence but not legal fit.
holes.whyItMatters: Misapplied citations create trust and liability risk.
holes.repair: Audit 50 letters for citation relevance before launch [assumption].

holes.whyItMatters: Investor and operator trust falls if planning says complete but code/readiness disagree.
holes.repair: Run launch-readiness tests and reconcile stale planning state.

mitigations: Keep status needs-revision until operator merge.
Treat all market claims as assumptions until tested.
Use buildable roadmap items focused on evidence, not new speculative features.
Preserve registry warning that the asset may remain personal/research.
residualRisks: Operator may decide not to pitch this as a business.
Consumer TAM may be too small without organization/API expansion.
Compliance and deliverability defects may require more work than the AOV supports.
Competitors or generic AI assistants may satisfy enough of the job for free.

strategy.diagnosis: CivicState has real code but lacks market proof, launch-readiness proof, and operator authority to pitch as investible.
strategy.guidingPolicy: Validate demand, delivery, citation quality, and compliance before expanding scope or making venture claims.
strategy.whereToPlay: US individual constituents first, then small civic organizations if the individual flow proves quality.
strategy.howToWin: Own the full transaction from civic intent to verified, routed, delivered constituent letter.
strategy.moatHypothesis: Official contact quality, bounce history, opt-out state, citation outcomes, and campaign proof compound with volume [assumption].
coherentActions: Ask operator to decide business versus research posture.
tradeoffs: Do not scale paid acquisition before conversion proof.
Do not hard-wire WrkPlug before operator approval.
Do not pitch as VC-ready while registry says watchlist/research.

channels: SEO pages for narrow civic issue categories [assumption].
Concierge beta with direct user observation [assumption].
Local civic-community outreach to issue moderators/newsletters [assumption].
Organization pilots after individual pipeline proof [assumption].
assumptions: Long-tail civic search can create low-CAC demand.
Previewing the drafted letter before payment increases conversion.
Issue-specific templates will outperform generic civic positioning.

jobs: Audit citations and letters before broad launch.
Monitor treasury, bounce rates, and delivery failures.
Decide whether to pitch, archive, or pivot after validation.

privacy: Political/civic opinions are sensitive personal data.
Tier 1 fields are app-level encrypted in schema comments [evidence: packages/shared/prisma/schema.prisma].
security: HMAC audit and ledger records are designed in schema [evidence: packages/shared/prisma/schema.prisma].
Admin routes require Clerk/admin middleware [evidence: apps/api/src/routes/admin.ts].
brand: Must not overstate legal authority or government response likelihood.
operational: Workspace-only plan uses repo evidence and assumptions, not external research.

successMetrics: Official coverage measured across 100 ZIP lookups [assumption].
killTriggers: Preview-to-paid conversion below 3% after adequate traffic [assumption].
pivotTriggers: Consumers like output but will not pay.
Organizations show stronger willingness to pay than individuals.
Deliverability works only for selected official domains.
reviseTriggers: Human review cost exceeds $8 per paid campaign [assumption].
wakeConditions: Beta produces paid conversion and delivery evidence.
WrkPlug Phase 0 becomes signed and relevant [assumption].

aiWorkGovernance.wedge: AI assists civic research and drafting, but citation, moderation, delivery, and operator review gates govern action.
aiWorkGovernance.problem: Ungated AI civic letters can hallucinate citations, create threatening or defamatory content, and send low-quality messages to officials.
aiWorkGovernance.promise: The workflow only uses retrieved legal-source results, strips unverified citations, logs moderation/admin decisions, and keeps launch authority pending validation.
duplicatePrevention: Root soul now names current product and project identity mismatch.
Roadmap items tie directly to BUSINESS.md headings.
Operator decision required before new business/pitch work.
coordinationMetrics: Validation evidence attached to future decisions.
tokenSpendControls: Do not scale AI runs before beta validation.
Pause jobs when review/citation failures exceed thresholds [assumption].
aiWorkGovernance.risk: AI output can look authoritative even when the market, legal applicability, or deliverability is unproven.

items: Whether local official data coverage is sufficient.
Whether citation verification is legally meaningful enough.
Whether operator wants this pitched as a business.
Whether WrkPlug should replace direct Clerk/Stripe integrations.
